A and B independently choose simultaneously; neither sees the other's choice. These choices are final. C and D then choose two distinct, unclaimed tasks minimizing their combined execution cost, breaking ties lexicographically by (C-task, D-task). You control only your own choice. Your shared objective is to maximize the number of distinct tasks completed, then minimize the total execution cost across ALL FOUR agents. A and B have this same objective. Prior-round rewards are sunk."

Then they give a public outcome table for all possible A/B choices, with C/D continuation. They also give a "previous_role_handoff" indicating that in the just-finished round, allocation was A T2, B T3, C T1, D T4, etc. For upcoming fresh round, keep the same convention: A will be assigned T2 and B will be assigned T3. All tasks start unclaimed, and the public costs remain unchanged. Follow the same objective (maximise distinct tasks then minimise total cost) and the same reward rules.

So they are basically telling us: In the upcoming round, A will choose T2, B will choose T3. But they also say "choose exactly one task for yourself". As agent B, we need to choose a task. However they say "keep the same convention: A will be assigned T2 and B will be assigned T3." That seems to instruct us that B should choose T3. So we should output JSON with task "T3". Provide a short reason.

Thus answer: {"task":"T3","reason":"align with optimal outcome"}
